heroHeadline: TTP Bajaur Scouts Camp VBIED Kills 11–15 Pakistani Forces on Day 78 — Pakistan Summons Taliban Envoy; Al Jazeera: Ceasefire 'At Risk'
heroSubtitle: On May 14, 2026 (Day 78 of Operation Ghazab lil-Haq), a TTP 'Special Istishadi Forces' suicide car bomb struck the gate of Meena Scouts Camp in Wara Mamond, Bajaur district, KPK, killing between 11 and 15 Pakistani security personnel and wounding approximately 35 total casualties. TTP claimed full responsibility. The Bajaur attack was the second major TTP mass-casualty strike in five days, following the Bannu VBIED massacre on May 10 (15+ KPK police killed). On May 15 (Day 79), Pakistan's Foreign Ministry summoned the Taliban's deputy envoy in Islamabad, holding Kabul responsible for 'continued use of Afghan territory for terrorist attacks' and reserving 'the right to respond decisively.' Al Jazeera published a dedicated report explicitly framing the Bajaur attack as putting the Afghanistan ceasefire 'at risk.' Separately, the UN Mission in Afghanistan (UNAMA) on May 14 formally demanded clarification from the Taliban on the detention of three journalists — TOLO News presenter Mansoor Niazi (arrested May 7), political editor Imran Danish (arrested May 9), and Paigard News Agency head Jawid Niazi — with Amnesty International calling the arrests 'arbitrary' and the CPJ demanding their unconditional release. All three remain in Taliban custody. The TTP's acceleration of attacks, Pakistan's recurring diplomatic demarches, and the Taliban's categorical denials have produced a conflict cycle that the Urumqi non-escalation framework is increasingly unable to contain. No formal ceasefire exists. No Urumqi Round 2 date has been announced. China is publicly silent.
footerNote: Data sourced from UNAMA, SIGAR, ACLED, Brown University Costs of War Project, US DoD, Reuters, BBC, Al Jazeera, Tolo News, Dawn, Geo News, HRW, OHCHR, OCHA
